neet_phy_u12_t08_1.working: Net emf = 4 × 1.5 = 6 V. Total internal resistance = 4 × 0.5 = 2 Ω. I = 6/(4+2) = 1.0 A.

neet_phy_u12_t08_2.working: With two cells reversed, net emf = (4−2) × 2 = 4 V. Internal resistance stays 6 × 0.5 = 3 Ω. I = 4/(7+3) = 0.4 A.

neet_phy_u12_t08_4.working: Series current = nε/(R+nr) ≈ nε/R. Parallel current = ε/(R + r/n) ≈ ε/R. So series gives the larger current and A is true. R correctly states why: the emf adds to nε in series while the resistance stays nearly R, but the emf remains ε in parallel.

neet_phy_u12_t08_5.working: I: circulating current = (3−1)/(1+1) = 1 A, so I is correct. II: net emf = (7−3) × 1.5 = 6 V, but internal resistance = 10 × 0.2 = 2 Ω, not 0.8 Ω, so II is incorrect.
